items.prompt: Ravi earned ₹3,600 as simple interest on ₹12,000 in 5 years. If he now invests ₹15,000 for 4 years at a rate 2% per annum higher than before, what simple interest will he earn?

solution.trap: ₹3,600 is the interest at the old 6% rate; the new deposit earns 8%.

items.prompt: Aman invested ₹x at 8% per annum simple interest for 3 years and ₹(x + 2,000) at 10% per annum simple interest for 2 years. If the interests from the two investments are in the ratio 6 : 7, find x.

solution.trap: ₹7,000 is the second principal, x + 2,000; the question asks for x.

items.prompt: Mahesh invested equal sums in two schemes. Scheme A pays 8% per annum simple interest for 3 years and scheme B pays 6% per annum simple interest for 5 years. Scheme B gives him ₹1,500 more interest than scheme A. How much did he invest in each scheme?

steps: Scheme A gives 8 × 3 = 24% of the sum; scheme B gives 6 × 5 = 30% of the sum.
Difference = 30% − 24% = 6% of the sum = ₹1,500 → sum = 1,500 × 100 ÷ 6 = ₹25,000 in each scheme.
solution.trap: ₹50,000 is the total across both schemes; the question asks for the sum in each.

items.prompt: Ajay lent ₹(x + 4,000) to Bharat at 6% per annum and ₹x to Chetan at 8% per annum, both at simple interest and for the same period. If both loans earned equal interest, find x.

steps: Same time, so equal interest means principal × rate is equal: 6(x + 4,000) = 8x.
solution.shortcut: Principals are in the inverse ratio of rates, 8 : 6 = 4 : 3; the gap of 1 part = ₹4,000, so x = 3 parts = ₹12,000.
solution.trap: ₹16,000 is Bharat's loan, x + 4,000; the question asks for x.

items.prompt: The compound interest on a sum at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually, exceeds the simple interest on the same sum at 8% per annum for 2 years by ₹1,250. Find the sum.

steps: CI at 10% for 2 years = 21% of the sum; SI at 8% for 2 years = 16% of the sum.
solution.trap: ₹31,250 treats the 10% interest as simple (20% − 16% = 4%); compounding adds 1% more, giving 21%.

items.prompt: Sunita lent ₹40,000, a part at 8% per annum and the rest at 12% per annum, both at simple interest. The total interest she received at the end of 1 year was ₹4,240. How much did she lend at 12%?

solution.trap: ₹14,000 is the part at 8%; the question asks for the part at 12%.

items.prompt: A sum of money invested at compound interest, compounded annually, amounts to ₹24,200 in 2 years and to ₹26,620 in 3 years. Find the sum.

solution.shortcut: Going back one year divides by 1.1: 24,200 → 22,000 → 20,000.
solution.trap: ₹19,360 subtracts ₹2,420 twice (simple-interest thinking); under compound interest each year's interest is smaller than the next.

items.prompt: A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. Find the rate of interest per annum.

steps: Doubling means the interest equals the principal, i.e. 100% of the sum in 8 years.
solution.trap: 25% would make the interest 200% of the sum (amount = 3 times); doubling needs interest of only 100%.

items.prompt: Rohan invested ₹15,000 at 8% per annum simple interest for 5 years. He then invested the entire amount at 10% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, for 2 years. Find the compound interest he earned.

solution.trap: ₹3,150 applies the CI to the original ₹15,000; the whole amount ₹21,000 was reinvested.

items.prompt: Kavita deposited ₹20,000 in a bank that pays compound interest at 10% for the first year and 12% for the second year. What amount will she receive at the end of 2 years?

solution.trap: ₹24,400 adds 10% + 12% = 22% simply; the second year's 12% is also earned on the first year's interest.

items.prompt: Prakash borrowed ₹40,000 at 8% per annum simple interest and lent the same sum at 10% per annum compound interest, compounded annually. What is his gain at the end of 2 years?

solution.trap: ₹1,600 treats the lending side as simple interest too (20% − 16%); it is compounded, so it earns 21%.

items.prompt: In how many years will ₹14,000 earn ₹4,200 as simple interest at 6% per annum?

solution.trap: Find the yearly interest first: 6% of ₹14,000 is ₹840, so 4 years gives only ₹3,360 and 6 years gives ₹5,040.

items.prompt: The simple interest on a sum for 3 years at 8% per annum is ₹4,800. Find the compound interest on the same sum at the same rate for 2 years, compounded annually.

solution.trap: ₹3,200 is the simple interest for 2 years; CI adds 8% of the first year's ₹1,600, i.e. ₹128 more.

items.prompt: Seema invested ₹x in scheme A at 12% per annum simple interest for 2 years and ₹(x − 3,000) in scheme B at 9% per annum simple interest for 4 years. The interests from schemes A and B are in the ratio 4 : 5. Find x.

steps: Interest from A = 24% of x = 0.24x; from B = 36% of (x − 3,000) = 0.36x − 1,080.
solution.trap: ₹15,000 is the amount in scheme B (x − 3,000), not x.

items.prompt: Naveen invested ₹x at 10% per annum simple interest for 4 years and ₹(x + 2,000) at 12% per annum simple interest for 3 years. The second investment earned ₹480 more interest than the first. Find x.

solution.trap: ₹30,000 solves 0.4x − (0.36x + 720) = 480, i.e. makes the FIRST interest larger; the question says the second is larger.

items.prompt: The simple interest on ₹x at 9% per annum for 4 years is equal to the simple interest on ₹(x + 6,000) at 7.5% per annum for 3 years. Find x.

solution.trap: ₹16,000 is the second principal, x + 6,000; the question asks for x.

items.prompt: Divya invested equal sums in two plans. Plan P pays 12% per annum simple interest for 3 years, and plan Q pays 10% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, for 2 years. Plan P gave her ₹2,700 more than plan Q. How much did she invest in each plan?

steps: Plan P: 12 × 3 = 36% of the sum. Plan Q: 10% compounded for 2 years = 21% of the sum.
36% − 21% = 15% of the sum = ₹2,700 → sum = ₹18,000 in each plan.
solution.trap: ₹16,875 treats plan Q as simple interest (20%), giving 36% − 20% = 16%; compounding makes plan Q earn 21%.

items.prompt: Neha earned ₹6,480 as simple interest on ₹18,000 in 4 years. At a rate 3% per annum higher than this, what simple interest would ₹22,500 earn in 5 years?

solution.trap: ₹10,125 keeps the old 9% rate; the new deposit earns 12%.

items.prompt: Find the simple interest on ₹7,500 at 9% per annum for 3 years 4 months.

solution.trap: ₹2,295 reads 3 years 4 months as 3.4 years; 4 months is 4/12 = 1/3 of a year.

items.prompt: ₹45,000 is divided into two parts. The first part is lent at 10% per annum simple interest for 4 years and the second part at 10% per annum simple interest for 6 years. If the two amounts received are equal, find the first part.

steps: Amount of first = 1.4 × first part; amount of second = 1.6 × second part.
solution.shortcut: Parts are in the inverse ratio of the amount factors: 160 : 140 = 8 : 7.
solution.trap: ₹21,000 is the second part: the part lent for the shorter time must be the larger one to reach the same amount.

items.prompt: Ritu invested ₹P in scheme A at 10% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, for 2 years, and ₹(P + 5,000) in scheme B at 8% per annum simple interest for 3 years. The interests from schemes A and B are in the ratio 7 : 9. Find P.

steps: Interest A = 21% of P = 0.21P; interest B = 24% of (P + 5,000) = 0.24P + 1,200.
solution.trap: ₹45,000 is scheme B's principal (P + 5,000); the question asks for P.

items.prompt: Out of ₹60,000, Harish lent a part at 6% per annum and the rest at 10% per annum, both at simple interest. The total interest he received in 3 years was ₹15,120. How much did he lend at 6%?

solution.trap: ₹36,000 is the part lent at 10%; the question asks for the part at 6%.

items.prompt: A sum of money at compound interest, compounded annually, amounts to ₹10,000 in 2 years and to ₹12,500 in 3 years. Find the sum.

steps: Interest in the 3rd year = 12,500 − 10,000 = ₹2,500 on ₹10,000 → rate = 25%.
solution.shortcut: Rate 25% = 1/4, so each year the amount is 5/4 of the year before: 10,000 × 4/5 × 4/5 = ₹6,400.
solution.trap: ₹7,500 subtracts ₹2,500 for each of 2 years as if interest were simple; ₹8,000 goes back only one year.

items.prompt: Arjun invested ₹32,000 at 12.5% per annum simple interest for 4 years. He then invested only the interest he earned at 20% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, for 2 years. Find the compound interest on this second investment.

solution.trap: ₹21,120 reinvests the whole amount ₹48,000; the question says only the interest was reinvested. ₹6,400 uses simple interest (40%) for the second step.

items.prompt: On a deposit of ₹15,000, a bank pays compound interest at 8% for the first year and 15% for the second year. Find the compound interest for the 2 years.

solution.trap: ₹3,450 adds 8% + 15% = 23% simply and misses the 15% earned on the first year's ₹1,200 (₹180).
